summary: The login error is macOS Security.framework errSecMissingEntitlement (-34018) from Data Protection Keychain access.

checks.observation: The screenshot reports error code -34018 and 'A required entitlement isn't present', matching the macOS missing-entitlement error.
ApiClient configures flutter_secure_storage with usesDataProtectionKeychain: true on macOS.
The app is ad-hoc signed and this host has no valid Apple code-signing identity.

Adding keychain-access-groups to both macOS entitlement files makes Xcode reject the build because this entitlement requires a development signing certificate. The temporary entitlement edits were reverted.
No signed macOS build was available to validate secure session write/read and relaunch. The known default legacy-Keychain service previously blocked in SecItemCopyMatching (QA-40).

Switched ad-hoc macOS builds to the package-supported legacy Keychain mode with an app-specific service name, isolating new sessions from the old default-service item without deleting it or requiring Keychain Sharing entitlement. Targeted auth/session tests and flutter analyze pass; flutter build macos --debug succeeds; flutter run -d macos launches and completes startup without the missing-entitlement exception.

next_step: On the running macOS client, complete a successful login, verify cookie storage does not raise PlatformException, quit and relaunch, and confirm the session restores. Existing cookies in the old default Keychain service are intentionally left untouched and require one re-login.
